unit: esc-045 control (a): the NULL BAND of the paired gradient-cosine statistic, measured BEFORE any arm difference is read (docs/maintainer/fine-tune-performance-guide.md section 6; .jammi/escapes.jsonl esc-045 row, control (a)). At the SAME 6 b4-s128 operating points row 11/s4:42's table covers (seeds 42/43/44 x {gaussian, poststep}), the IDENTICAL statistic run_esc045_torch_column.sh's own table reports -- full_tensor_cosine(bf16_arm, jammi_f32_truth), the 224-tensor concatenated cosine analyze_esc045_torch_column.py's compare_arm_vs_truth computes, imported unchanged -- is computed TWICE per (arm, operating point): two independent process invocations of the IDENTICAL command (same seed, same --lora-weights-in shared safetensors file, same batch/config, same jammi_f32_truth dump reused for both). The paired difference (repA - repB) and its sign are reported per point, then the sign test over the 6 points, for torch-vs-torch and jammi-eager-vs-jammi-eager.

replicate_design.chosen_nuisance: run-to-run nondeterminism only (independent process reruns of the identical CLI invocation)
replicate_design.justification: grad_oracle.rs's own determinant table (module doc, 'Determinant table -- every field either producer emits, classified') marks seed, batch, seq, lora_rank, lora_alpha, target_modules, batched_forward, backbone_dtype, checkpoint_config_sha256, checkpoint_weights_sha256, checkpoint_weights_size_bytes, lora_weights_in (presence), batch_token_id_sums, and lora_init as IDENTITY fields -- pinned equal between the two REAL arms esc-045's own table compares (block/flash/eager-jammi vs torch_bf16), since both load the IDENTICAL LoRA weights via the shared safetensors interchange file and the SAME synthetic batch (grad_oracle.rs module doc, 'Weight interchange format': 'this is the crux: it removes the init mismatch ENTIRELY, on both the value and the bit level'). A replicate that varied LoRA init or the data seed between repA/repB would therefore inject a nuisance the REAL between-arm comparison never carries -- an apples-to-oranges null band, not this control's null band. The ONLY thing left that can legitimately differ between two runs at an otherwise fully-pinned operating point is run-to-run nondeterminism in that arm's OWN kernel execution (GPU reduction-order / algorithm-selection variability) -- which is the SAME CATEGORY of nuisance (floating-point accumulation-order variability in a bf16 forward+backward) that separates two INDEPENDENTLY-IMPLEMENTED bf16 backward paths (torch's vs jammi's) at a shared operating point. This is the design run_esc045_null_band.sh/analyze_esc045_null_band.py implement.
replicate_design.second_replicate_considered_and_rejected: Toggling --batched-forward (single joined 3b-row forward vs three separate per-group forwards) was considered as a second, mechanistically different nuisance: it changes GEMM/reduction grouping while holding seed/weights/batch content identical, and grad_oracle.rs's own test grad_oracle_batched_and_unbatched_forward_agree documents this is NOT bit-exact (~1e-6 relative, reduction-order noise). It was REJECTED as a null-band replicate here: batched_forward IS a RUN_IDENTITY_FIELDS entry in compare_grad_oracle.py, and BOTH real arms in esc-045's own table hold it fixed identically (True, the default, on every leg of run_esc045_torch_column.sh) -- so varying it between repA/repB would, like a different init draw, inject a nuisance the real between-arm comparison never carries. It does not satisfy this control's own 'same nuisance that varies between arms' criterion and was not run.

second_null_actually_run.chosen_nuisance: torch --attn eager vs --attn sdpa (same torch/PEFT stack, same checkpoint, same IDENTICAL shared LoRA weights file, same batch, same bf16 dtype -- ONLY the attention kernel implementation differs). Run at the coordinator's direction as a second, mechanistically closer null: unlike the pure process-rerun null above (which only exercises launch-to-launch determinism of the IDENTICAL code path), this null exercises a genuinely DIFFERENT attention-kernel implementation within ONE well-tested framework -- closer in kind to 'a different implementation computes the attention op' than a bare process rerun is, even though it is still not a perfect analog of jammi-vs-torch (both sdpa and eager here are torch's own kernels).

eager_arm_dispatch_evidence.mechanism: Every jammi_bf16_eager leg ran with JAMMI_KERNELS_DISABLE=all JAMMI_KERNELS_STRICT=1. Verified directly against all 12 raw dumps (2 replicates x 6 operating points): every one of the 7 named op-family *_fused_dispatches counters (ln, rope, softmax, geglu, lora_epilogue, lora_linear, attention_block) reads EXACTLY 0 on every leg, kernels_disabled_requested == kernels_disabled_fired == ['all'] on every leg (the disable actually took effect, not merely requested), and eager dispatch counts are nonzero and IDENTICAL across repA/repB at each operating point (ln=57, rope=56, softmax=28, geglu=28, lora_linear=112, attention_block=28; lora_epilogue=0 on both arms/reps -- a registered-but-not-independently-dispatched key at this call site, per grad_oracle.rs's own live_admit_keys doc).

paired_table.description: Per (config, op_point), the full-tensor cosine of dL/dB vs jammi_f32_truth for TWO independent process replicates of each arm (torch_bf16, jammi_bf16_eager), their paired difference (repA - repB), sign, and the resulting sign test over the 6 b4-s128 operating points row 11/s4:42's table covers. NO cross-arm verdict is computed here -- this artifact answers ONLY 'is the paired-sign statistic itself chaotic under run-to-run nondeterminism', control (a) of the esc-045 ledger row.

null_A_process_nondeterminism.reading: Under the run-to-run-nondeterminism-only replicate design (the only nuisance that does not violate the 'same nuisance the real arms carry' constraint), BOTH torch_bf16 and jammi_bf16_eager are BIT-FOR-BIT DETERMINISTIC across independent process invocations at every one of the 6 operating points -- confirmed both via the analyzer's full-float64 paired diff (exactly 0.0, not a rounding artifact) and via a raw byte-level diff of the two repA/repB dumps at seed42/gaussian (jammi's two dumps are byte-IDENTICAL; torch's two dumps differ in exactly one field, the ISO-8601 date_utc provenance timestamp -- confirmed by diffing with that one line stripped). The null band is therefore EXACTLY 0.000000000 for both arms at every point, strictly narrower than every one of the 6 block-vs-torch deficits in the existing table (magnitudes 0.008 .. 0.749). The sign counts are 0 positive / 0 negative / 6 zero (a degenerate tie, not a directional 6/6) for BOTH arms -- this is NOT the 'consistent 6/6 same-direction sign' pattern the control's own RED criterion describes, so this control does not find the paired-sign statistic to be an artifact of run-to-run nondeterminism. esc-045's block-vs-torch 6/6 sign stands with respect to THIS control. Scope: this control only rules out run-to-run GPU/kernel nondeterminism as the source of the cross-arm sign pattern; it does not by itself settle whether that pattern reflects a real defect vs an inherent (but reproducible) sensitivity of bf16 gradient direction to which stack computed it, and it does not touch esc-046's rounding confound or control (d)'s forced-defect positive control -- both remain open per the ledger row.

null_B_torch_eager_vs_sdpa.reading: Switching JUST the attention kernel implementation within torch's own stack (eager -> sdpa), holding weights/batch/dtype fixed, produces a STRONGLY skewed paired sign: 5 negative / 1 positive over the same 6 operating points (not the 6/6 the block arm shows, but far from an even ~3/3 split either). Magnitudes range 0.049-0.222. 5 of the 6 block-vs-eager deficits (0.008, 0.116, 0.125, 0.149, 0.186) sit AT OR BELOW this null's own max magnitude (0.222) -- indistinguishable in size from ordinary within-framework attention-kernel-choice variance at this metric/shape. Only the seed44/gaussian point (0.749) clearly exceeds anything NULL B produced. Reading: NULL B is NOT the clean, vacuous 6/6 the escape's own RED criterion describes, so it does not, by itself, declare the paired-sign statistic fully chaotic either -- but it substantially weakens the case that esc-045's cross-framework 6/6 (block-fused jammi vs torch-eager) is diagnostic of a jammi-specific defect rather than ordinary bf16-attention-kernel-implementation sensitivity that ALSO appears purely within torch. Combined with NULL A (which rules out pure process nondeterminism), the honest overall picture is: the paired-sign statistic is NOT chaotic from run-to-run noise, but IS substantially noisy with respect to WHICH attention-kernel implementation computes the op -- at 5/6 of the 6 points, the observed block-arm deficit is not distinguishable in magnitude from that noise source alone.

red_green_reading.overall: MIXED, not a clean GREEN. NULL A (process rerun) rules out run-to-run GPU/kernel nondeterminism entirely (exactly 0 variance) -- on that axis, esc-045's 6/6 is not vacuous. NULL B (attention-implementation swap within torch itself) shows a strongly skewed but not unanimous sign (5/6 negative) with magnitudes overlapping 5 of the 6 block-vs-eager deficits -- on that axis, esc-045's cross-framework 6/6 sign is not clearly distinguishable from ordinary implementation-choice noise at most of the 6 points; only seed44/gaussian (0.749) stands out. This does not retract esc-045 as valid-defect-on-the-paired-statistic (the ledger's own framing) -- it sharpens the open question the ledger row already names: the closing instrument is a learning curve, not another cosine bisect, and this control's own finding is additional evidence for why a single-step cosine sign at this shape has limited resolving power.

known_limitations.description: Determinism is measured on ONE box (a100d, A100-SXM4-80GB, driver 580.126.16) with SAME-PROCESS-family reruns (repA/repB launched sequentially from the same script, same box, same driver/cuda-toolkit version, same checkpoint bytes). This rules out run-to-run nondeterminism ON THIS BOX under these conditions; it does not claim cross-box/cross-driver bit-reproducibility (out of scope for control (a), which is about the metric's OWN resolving power on a single measurement apparatus, not cross-box portability -- see guide section 8's own box-identity discipline for why that is a separate question).

jammi_f32_truth is generated ONCE per (config, op_point) and reused for BOTH replicates' cosine, by design (this module's own doc: 'f32 accumulation order is not the noise source under test'). If f32 accumulation itself carried run-to-run nondeterminism at this shape, this design would not detect it -- considered unlikely (f32 GEMM/reduction paths are the same deterministic cuBLAS/candle call sites as bf16's, just at higher precision) but not independently verified this round.

cargo test -p jammi-bench on this box (a100d, nvidia-smi present) reports 100 passed, 1 failed: finetune_step::tests::finetune_step_peak_vram_bytes_is_not_yet_measured_off_gpu panics at finetune_step.rs:1544 ('no nvidia-smi on this box => VramSampler::start() returns None => peak_vram_bytes must be the not-yet-measured sentinel, never a fabricated 0.0' -- left: Some(0.0), right: None). This is a KNOWN pre-existing defect (the test's own name/premise is 'off_gpu': it asserts CPU-only behaviour but fails on ANY box that has nvidia-smi, including every real GPU pod), tracked and fixed on the separate #381 branch -- NOT caused by this dispatch (zero Rust source files were touched by bench/esc045-null-band) and NOT fixed here; #381 owns the fix. The gate-runner script that captured this exit code also had its own bug, independently caught: `cargo test ... | tee log; echo TEST_EXIT=$?` captures tee's exit status (0), not cargo test's, so the log's own TEST_EXIT=0 line is wrong -- the correct exit code (1) was read off the actual `test result: FAILED. 100 passed; 1 failed` line in the same log, not off the miscaptured $?. Any future gate script on this branch's lineage must use PIPESTATUS[0] (bash) after a `| tee`, not a bare $?.
